scenes.say: Docker talks about images and containers, but what’s the key difference you need to know?

scenes.prompt: A cargo ship stacked with identical sealed containers, dock workers unloading containers onto the port, each container being opened and used. Sunny port, cranes, busy workers.
scenes.say: Think of a cargo ship: images are sealed containers, ready to ship. Running containers are those opened and used on the dock.

scenes.label: Image
scenes.sub: A read-only template built in layers.
scenes.say: An image is a read-only template, built in layers. It’s not running yet.

scenes.label: Container
scenes.sub: A running instance with its own writable layer.
scenes.say: A container is a running instance of that image, with its own thin writable layer on top.

scenes.code:
$ docker run nginx
# Starts a container from the image
scenes.say: When you run an image, Docker creates a container. One image can run many containers.

scenes.question: Is an image a running container?
scenes.right: No. An image is the template; a container is the running instance with its own writable layer.
scenes.say: Don’t confuse the two. An image is just the template. A container is the running instance, with its own writable layer.
